      "species": [],

      "n_counts": "diseases in the human DO",
      "verbatim": "Only a small fraction of the 11,158 diseases curated in the human DO have been investigated in drug development (14%; 1549 out of 11,158 diseases) or GWAS (17%; 1914 out of 11,158 diseases);"
    },
    {
      "statistic": "coverage",
      "value": 17.0,
      "unit": "percent",
      "measures": "diseases that have been investigated by GWAS",
      "compared": "diseases in the human DO vs. diseases investigated by GWAS",
      "species": [],
      "n": 11158,
      "n_counts": "diseases in the human DO",
      "verbatim": "Only a small fraction of the 11,158 diseases curated in the human DO have been investigated in drug development (14%; 1549 out of 11,158 diseases) or GWAS (17%; 1914 out of 11,158 diseases);"
    },
    {
      "statistic": "overlap",
      "value": 47.0,
      "unit": "percent",
      "measures": "diseases being pursued in clinical phase drug development that have also been the subject of a GWAS",
      "compared": "diseases in clinical phase drug development vs. diseases studied by GWAS",
      "species": [],
      "n": 1401,
      "n_counts": "diseases being pursued in clinical phase drug development",
      "verbatim": "Of diseases being pursued in clinical phase drug development, only 47% have been the subject of a GWAS (661 out of 1401);"
    },
    {
      "statistic": "coverage",
      "value": 13.9,
      "unit": "percent",
      "measures": "unique diseases that have an approved drug and/or a drug under clinical or preclinical development",
      "compared": "total number of human diseases in DO vs. diseases with approved or developing drugs",
      "species": [],
      "n": 11158,
      "n_counts": "total number of human diseases in DO",
      "verbatim": "By sourcing data from the ChEMBL v31 35 , we found that only 1549 unique diseases (estimated as 13.9% of the total number of human diseases in DO) have an approved drug and/or a drug under clinical or preclinical development."
    },
    {
      "statistic": "coverage",
      "value": 17.2,
      "unit": "percent",
      "measures": "diseases covered by GWAS",
      "compared": "total number of common human diseases vs. diseases covered by GWAS",
      "species": [],
      "n": 11158,
      "n_counts": "total number of common human diseases",
      "verbatim": "Nevertheless, with these caveats, we identified 1914 diseases covered by GWAS (17.2% of the total number of common human diseases) based on the mapping and manual curation of phenotype terms in the GWAS Catalog 43 and UK Biobank 38 to UMLS concepts (Supplementary Data 5 )."
    },
    {
      "statistic": "overlap",
      "value": 2.5,
      "unit": "percent",
      "measures": "unique target-indication pairings explored in drug development within the space of clinical investigation",
      "compared": "target-indication pairings explored in drug development vs. all target-indication pairings under clinical investigation",
      "species": [],
      "n": 1706418,
      "n_counts": "target-indication pairings under clinical investigation",
      "verbatim": "Within this bounded space of ~1.7 million target indication pairings within sample space ‘ C ’, only 42,199 unique target-indication pairings (2.5%) have been explored in drug development."
    },
    {
      "statistic": "coverage",
      "value": 1.0,
      "unit": "percent",
      "measures": "drug target-disease indication hypotheses explored and led to approval within the bounded space of approved drugs",
      "compared": "drug target-disease indication hypotheses leading to approval vs. maximum possible space for approved drugs",
      "species": [],
      "n": 462060,
      "n_counts": "maximum space for approved drugs",
      "verbatim": "Of these, the number of drug target-disease indication hypotheses that have been explored and led to approval within this bounded space is 5221 (1% of the maximum space, Supplementary Data 1 )."
    },
    {
      "statistic": "overlap",
      "value": 73.9,
      "unit": "percent",
      "measures": "genes encoding druggable targets that are currently 'undrugged'",
      "compared": "genes encoding druggable targets vs. genes encoding undrugged targets",
      "species": [],
      "n": 4729,
      "n_counts": "genes encoding druggable targets",
      "verbatim": "Of all human genes encoding druggable targets, 755 (16%) are already the targets of approved drugs, 1218 (26%) are the targets of drugs in clinical development, 418 (9%) are targets of drugs in preclinical development, with 3495 (73.9%) being currently ‘undrugged’ (Fig. 1 , Supplementary Data 1 )."
    },
    {
      "statistic": "overlap",
      "value": 16.0,
      "unit": "percent",
      "measures": "genes encoding druggable targets that are targets of approved drugs",
      "compared": "genes encoding druggable targets vs. genes encoding targets of approved drugs",
      "species": [],
      "n": 4729,
      "n_counts": "genes encoding druggable targets",
      "verbatim": "Of all human genes encoding druggable targets, 755 (16%) are already the targets of approved drugs, 1218 (26%) are the targets of drugs in clinical development, 418 (9%) are targets of drugs in preclinical development, with 3495 (73.9%) being currently ‘undrugged’ (Fig. 1 , Supplementary Data 1 )."
    },
    {
      "statistic": "overlap",
      "value": 26.0,
      "unit": "percent",
      "measures": "genes encoding druggable targets that are targets of drugs in clinical development",
      "compared": "genes encoding druggable targets vs. genes encoding targets of drugs in clinical development",
      "species": [],
      "n": 4729,
      "n_counts": "genes encoding druggable targets",
      "verbatim": "Of all human genes encoding druggable targets, 755 (16%) are already the targets of approved drugs, 1218 (26%) are the targets of drugs in clinical development, 418 (9%) are targets of drugs in preclinical development, with 3495 (73.9%) being currently ‘undrugged’ (Fig. 1 , Supplementary Data 1 )."
    },
    {
      "statistic": "overlap",
      "value": 9.0,
      "unit": "percent",
      "measures": "genes encoding druggable targets that are targets of drugs in preclinical development",
      "compared": "genes encoding druggable targets vs. genes encoding targets of drugs in preclinical development",
      "species": [],
      "n": 4729,
      "n_counts": "genes encoding druggable targets",
      "verbatim": "Of all human genes encoding druggable targets, 755 (16%) are already the targets of approved drugs, 1218 (26%) are the targets of drugs in clinical development, 418 (9%) are targets of drugs in preclinical development, with 3495 (73.9%) being currently ‘undrugged’ (Fig. 1 , Supplementary Data 1 )."
    },
    {
      "statistic": "overlap",
      "value": 5.5,
      "unit": "percent",
      "measures": "diseases with currently approved drugs that have also been studied in GWAS",
      "compared": "diseases with approved drugs vs. diseases studied by GWAS",
      "species": [],
      "n": 11158,
      "n_counts": "total diseases",
      "verbatim": "We identified 755 targets of currently approved drugs (16% of all druggable targets) employed in the treatment of 612 diseases (5.5% of all 11,158 diseases). Of these diseases, 336 have also been studied in GWAS."
    },
    {
      "statistic": "overlap",
      "value": 47.0,
      "unit": "percent",
      "measures": "disease indications being evaluated in clinical development that have previously been the subject of a GWAS",
      "compared": "disease indications in clinical development vs. disease indications previously studied by GWAS",
      "species": [],
      "n": 1401,
      "n_counts": "disease indications being evaluated in clinical development",
      "verbatim": "However, of the 1401 disease indications being evaluated in clinical development, only 661 have previously been the subject of a GWAS."
    },
    {
      "statistic": "overlap",
      "value": 363.0,
      "unit": "count",
      "measures": "diseases that have approved treatment and have been studied by a GWAS, among those not having approved treatment but being evaluated in clinical development",
      "compared": "diseases in clinical development without approved treatment that have been studied by GWAS vs. all diseases in clinical development without approved treatment",
      "species": [],
      "n": 925,
      "n_counts": "diseases in clinical development without approved treatment",
      "verbatim": "Of these 1401 disease indications, 476 have already approved treatment, and of the remaining 925 diseases, 363 have been studied by a GWAS."
    }
  ],
  "headline_index": 0,
  "what_the_study_did": "The study systematically mapped drug development and genomic discovery efforts in common diseases to produce target-disease indication lists.",
  "what_it_found": "The study found that only a small fraction of human diseases have been investigated in drug development or GWAS, and that the overlap between diseases being pursued in clinical drug development and those studied by GWAS is less than half.",
  "key_quotes": [
    {
      "quote": "Pre-clinical, cell and animal model-based approaches for drug target identification and validation have been poorly predictive of human efficacy, contributing to the high failure rate in clinical phase drug development 1 – 3 due to lack of benefit or unanticipated adverse effects 4 , 5 .",
      "topic": "Predictive limitations"
    },
    {
      "quote": "We find that only 5% of the diseases have an approved drug treatment in at least one region of the world and that less than half of the diseases that pharmaceutical companies are currently attempting to develop drugs for have been investigated by GWAS.",
      "topic": "Low coverage"
    },
    {
      "quote": "In addition, approximately two-thirds of the diseases investigated using genetic studies have yet to be investigated in drug development.",
      "topic": "GWAS vs. drug dev"
    },
    {
      "quote": "Only a small fraction of the 11,158 diseases curated in the human DO have been investigated in drug development (14%; 1549 out of 11,158 diseases) or GWAS (17%; 1914 out of 11,158 diseases);",
      "topic": "Disease investigation"
    },
    {
      "quote": "Of diseases being pursued in clinical phase drug development, only 47% have been the subject of a GWAS (661 out of 1401);",
      "topic": "Clinical development overlap"
    },
    {
      "quote": "Even for the 661 diseases that are the subject of ongoing clinical phase drug development and have been covered by GWAS, it remains uncertain how many of the specific target-indication pairings have genetic support.",
      "topic": "Target-indication uncertainty"
    }
  ]
}
